install.subtitle: Install {{brand}} to open it like any other app, with its own icon and window.
install.installNowHint: Your browser can install {{brand}} right away.
install.installed: You’re already using the installed app.

desktop.title: Windows, Mac or Linux computer
chromeSteps: Open {{brand}} in Chrome and sign in.
Click the install icon at the right end of the address bar (a small screen with a down arrow).
No icon? Open the ⋮ menu → Cast, save and share → Install page as app.
Click Install. {{brand}} opens in its own window and appears in your Start menu, Dock or app list.
edgeSteps: Open {{brand}} in Edge and sign in.
Click the App available icon in the address bar.
No icon? Open the … menu → Apps → Install this site as an app.
Click Install. You can pin it to the taskbar or Dock.
desktop.safariNote: Safari on a Mac (macOS Sonoma or later): choose File → Add to Dock.
desktop.firefoxNote: Firefox can’t install web apps. Open {{brand}} in Chrome or Edge to install it.

android.title: Android phone or tablet
steps: Tap the ⋮ menu at the top right.
Tap Install app (on some phones it says Add to Home screen).
Tap Install. The {{brand}} icon appears on your home screen.

ios.title: iPhone or iPad
steps: Tap the Share button (a square with an arrow pointing up).
Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen.
Tap Add. Then always open {{brand}} from the new icon.
ios.version: Needs iOS or iPadOS 16.4 or later.
ios.whyTitle: Why notifications need the Home Screen icon
ios.why: Apple only lets web apps send notifications after they are added to the Home Screen. In a normal Safari tab, {{brand}} can’t notify you. Open it from the Home Screen icon, then turn on notifications in Settings → Notifications.

faq.subtitle: Tap a question to see the answer.

otp.q: I didn’t get my sign-in code
points: Check your Spam or Junk folder. The code comes from {{email}}.
Wait 60 seconds before asking for a new code. You can ask for up to 5 codes an hour.
Only @{{domain}} email addresses can sign in.
A code works for 10 minutes. If it has expired, ask for a new one.

session.q: Why do I sign in again every 7 days?
session.a: For your security, each sign-in lasts 7 days, even if you use {{brand}} every day. After that, sign in again with a new code. You’ll see a reminder in the app 24 hours before.

notifications.q: How do I turn on notifications?
points: Go to Settings → Notifications and turn them on. When your browser asks, choose Allow.
On iPhone and iPad, notifications only work after you add {{brand}} to the Home Screen and open it from that icon.
Blocked them by mistake? Click the icon next to the web address and allow notifications for this site.
notifications.install: How to add to the Home Screen

microphone.intro: Voice notes need your microphone. To allow it:
microphone.chromium: Chrome or Edge: click the icon to the left of the web address → Site settings (or Permissions for this site) → Microphone → Allow. Then reload the page.
microphone.firefox: Firefox: click the microphone or lock icon in the address bar, clear the Blocked permission, and try again.
microphone.safari-mac: Safari on Mac: Safari → Settings → Websites → Microphone, and set {{brand}} to Allow.
microphone.ios: iPhone or iPad: open the Settings app → Safari → Microphone (on iOS 18: Settings → Apps → Safari), and choose Ask or Allow.
microphone.system: Still blocked? Your computer may block it too. Windows: Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone. Mac: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, and allow your browser.

storage.q: What does {{brand}} keep on my device?
points: {{brand}} keeps a copy of your chats in this browser, so you can read them offline and the app opens faster.
Clearing this site’s data signs you out on this browser. Your messages stay safe on our server and come back when you sign in again.
Photos, videos and documents can be up to {{size}} each.
storage.sizeUnknown: Photos, videos and documents have a size limit. The app tells you if a file is too big.

lost.q: I lost my phone or laptop
points: On another device, go to Settings → Devices.
Sign out the lost device, or choose Sign out all other devices.
Got a new sign-in email you don’t recognise? Click “This wasn’t me” in it: that signs you out everywhere.

account.a: Your account belongs to your organization, so you can’t delete it yourself. If you’re leaving, an admin will turn it off.

privacy.subtitle: In plain words: what we keep, and who can see it.
store: Your account: work email, name, @username, profile photo and “about”.
Your messages and files, on our server, so all your devices show the same chats.
The devices you sign in on (browser, device type, IP address, last active), so you can see them in Settings → Devices.
protect: Everything is encrypted on the way between your device and our server.
Files are private: only members of the chat can open them, through links that expire after 15 minutes.
Messages are not end-to-end encrypted yet. They are stored on our server in a form the server can read.
who: Only the members of a chat can see its messages and files.
You choose who sees your last seen, profile photo and read ticks in Settings → Privacy.
Admins can turn accounts off and review reports. There is no screen in the app that lets them open your chats.

When someone reports a person, group or message, a copy of the reported messages (and a few recent ones from that chat) is attached so an admin can check it. Opening a report is recorded in the audit log.
Because messages aren’t end-to-end encrypted, the people who run the server could technically get to stored data.
limits: Disappearing messages are removed after the time you pick. View once photos and videos can be opened only once.
A browser can’t block screenshots or screen recording. Someone could copy the text or photograph the screen before it disappears.
Only send what you’d be fine with the other person keeping.
lock: Chat lock hides chats behind your PIN, so someone using your unlocked device can’t read them. Your PIN works on all your devices.
It isn’t encryption: locked chats are stored on our server like any other chat.
